sentence: Direct: The clerk said to the candidate, "Are you ready for the skill test?"
correctAnswer: The clerk asked the candidate if he was ready for the skill test.

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type & Intent: Direct sentence Yes/No question hai jo auxiliary 'Are' se shuru ho raha hai aur confirmation pooch raha hai.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb & Connective: Reporting verb 'said to' ko question ke anusaar 'asked' mein badla, quotation marks hataye aur connective 'if' (ya 'whether') lagaya.
steps.step3_aspect: Pronoun Reference Shift: 2nd person pronoun 'you' listener 'the candidate' (singular) ke anusaar badal kar 'he' ban gaya.
steps.step4_inflection: Inversion Removal & Backshift: Auxiliary 'are' backshift hokar 'was' ban gayi aur inverted order hatakar subject 'he' ke baad aayi ('he was ready', NOT '*was he ready'). End ka question mark drop ho gaya.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The clerk asked the candidate if he was ready for the skill test.'

trapWarning: EXAM TRAP: Options mein aksar 'asked that if...' (double conjunction) ya 'if was he ready' (inversion retained) diya jata hai. Dono ko instantly eliminate karein.

sentence: Direct: The magistrate said to the witness, "Do you know the accused personally?"
correctAnswer: The magistrate asked the witness if he knew the accused personally.

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type & Intent: Auxiliary 'Do' se start hone wala interrogative sentence jo personal knowledge verify kar raha hai.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb & Connective: 'said to' ➔ 'asked the witness', aur question clause ko link karne ke liye connective 'if' lagaya.
steps.step3_aspect: Pronoun Reference Shift: 'you' listener 'the witness' ke anusaar 'he' ban gaya.
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary Removal & Past Inflection: Affirmative statement mein auxiliary 'do' drop ho jati hai aur main verb 'know' Simple Past form 'knew' (V2) mein badal jati hai.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The magistrate asked the witness if he knew the accused personally.'

trapWarning: FATAL 'DID KNOW' DISTRACTOR: Examiner aksar 'if he did know the accused' option deta hai. Normal affirmative reported clause mein 'did' nahi lagta, seedha V2 'knew' aata hai.

sentence: Direct: The police officer said to the guard, "Did you lock the court record room?"
correctAnswer: The police officer asked the guard whether he had locked the court record room.
tense: Yes/No Question with 'Did' Auxiliary (Simple Past ➔ Past Perfect)

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type & Tense: Question auxiliary 'Did' se shuru ho raha hai, jo Simple Past tense indicate karta hai.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb & Connective: 'said to' ➔ 'asked the guard', connective 'whether' lagaya.
steps.step3_aspect: Pronoun Reference Shift: 'you' listener 'the guard' ke anusaar 'he' ban gaya.
steps.step4_inflection: Tense Backshift: Simple Past ('did lock') backshift hokar Past Perfect ('had locked') ban gaya, aur subject 'he' auxiliary se pehle aaya.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The police officer asked the guard whether he had locked the court record room.'

trapWarning: TENSE RETENTION TRAP: Option mein agar 'whether he locked...' likha ho, toh wo Simple Past se Past Perfect mein backshift karne mein fail ho gaya hai. 'Had locked' wala option hi correct hai.

sentence: Direct: The judge said to the advocate, "Will you accept this compromise or not?"
correctAnswer: The judge asked the advocate whether or not he would accept that compromise.
tense: Interrogative with Explicit 'Or Not' Choice (Mandatory Whether)

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type & Structure: Interrogative sentence jisme explicit choice 'or not' directly judi huyi hai.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb & Connective: 'said to' ➔ 'asked the advocate'. 'Or not' aane ke karan connective 'whether' lagaya ('if' avoid kiya).
steps.step3_aspect: Pronoun Reference Shift: 'you' listener 'the advocate' ke anusaar 'he' ban gaya. Time/place demonstrative 'this' ➔ 'that'.
steps.step4_inflection: Modal Backshift & Syntax: Modal 'will' backshift hokar 'would' ban gaya: 'whether or not he would accept that compromise'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The judge asked the advocate whether or not he would accept that compromise.'

trapWarning: IF OR NOT TRAP: Option mein 'asked if or not he would accept...' standard examination English mein unacceptable maana jata hai. 'Whether or not' clean rule hai.

sentence: Direct: The inspector said to the clerk, "Where did you submit the original case dairy?"
correctAnswer: The inspector asked the clerk where he had submitted the original case dairy.
tense: Wh-Question (Where) with Simple Past ➔ Past Perfect

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type & Intent: Wh-interrogative sentence starting with 'Where', inquiring about location in past time.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb & Connective: 'said to' ➔ 'asked the clerk'. Original question word 'where' hi connective banega (NO 'that' / NO 'if').
steps.step3_aspect: Pronoun Reference Shift: 'you' listener 'the clerk' ke anusaar 'he' ban gaya.
steps.step4_inflection: Inversion Removal & Backshift: Simple Past ('did submit') backshift hokar Past Perfect ('had submitted') bana, aur subject 'he' auxiliary se pehle aaya: 'where he had submitted'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The inspector asked the clerk where he had submitted the original case dairy.'

trapWarning: INVERSION TRAP: Distractor option: 'where had he submitted...' (inversion retained). Yaad rakhein: reported question statement hota hai, isliye 'where he had submitted' aayega.

sentence: Direct: The senior counsel said to the junior, "Why are you arguing without reading the precedent?"
correctAnswer: The senior counsel asked the junior why he was arguing without reading the precedent.
tense: Wh-Question (Why) with Present Continuous ➔ Past Continuous

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type & Intent: Wh-question expressing reason/cause in Present Continuous aspect.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb & Connective: 'said to' ➔ 'asked the junior', 'why' connective bana.
steps.step3_aspect: Pronoun Reference Shift: 'you' junior (singular) ke anusaar 'he' ban gaya.
steps.step4_inflection: Tense Backshift: Present Continuous ('are arguing') backshift hokar Past Continuous ('was arguing') bana, subject 'he' pehle aaya.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The senior counsel asked the junior why he was arguing without reading the precedent.'

trapWarning: DOUBLE CONJUNCTION ALERT: Distractor mein 'asked the junior that why was he arguing...' hoga. 'That' aur inverted order dono galat hain.

sentence: Direct: The registrar said, "Who broke the seal of this confidential envelope?"
correctAnswer: The registrar enquired who had broken the seal of that confidential envelope.
tense: Wh-Question (Who) with Simple Past Subject Question

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type & Structure: 'Who' subject-question hai jisme 'Who' khud grammatical subject ka kaam kar raha hai.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb & Connective: Formal context ke anusaar 'enquired' lagaya, 'who' connective bana.
steps.step3_aspect: Adverbial Shift: Demonstrative 'this confidential envelope' ➔ 'that confidential envelope'.
steps.step4_inflection: Tense Backshift: Simple Past verb 'broke' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had broken' ban gayi.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The registrar enquired who had broken the seal of that confidential envelope.'

trapWarning: SUBJECT QUESTION SYNTAX: 'Who' wale question mein do/did nahi hota jab 'Who' subject ho. Iska indirect seedha 'who had broken' banega.

sentence: Direct: Rohan said to the official, "When will the typing test results be announced?"
correctAnswer: Rohan enquired of the official when the typing test results would be announced.
tense: Wh-Question with Formal 'Enquired of' Reporting Verb

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type & Intent: Official enquiry regarding future examination schedule.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb & Preposition: 'said to + object' ko formal inquiry ke anusaar 'enquired of the official' mein convert kiya (preposition 'of' mandatory hai).
steps.step3_aspect: Connective: 'when' connective retain hua, koi extra 'that' nahi joda.
steps.step4_inflection: Word Order & Modal Backshift: Subject 'the typing test results' pehle aaya, aur modal 'will' backshift hokar 'would' ban gaya.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'Rohan enquired of the official when the typing test results would be announced.'

trapWarning: MISSING 'OF' TRAP: Option mein 'Rohan enquired the official...' hoga. 'Enquired' listener object ke sath 'of' ke bina kabhi nahi aata.

sentence: Direct: The judge said to the court orderly, "Call the petitioner immediately."
correctAnswer: The judge ordered the court orderly to call the petitioner immediately.

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type & Hierarchy: Imperative sentence starting with base verb 'Call'. Speaker judge hai aur listener orderly hai (strict hierarchical command).
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb: 'said to' ko context ke anusaar 'ordered' mein convert kiya.
steps.step3_aspect: Listener Object: 'the court orderly' reporting verb ka direct object bana.
steps.step4_inflection: Infinitive Construction: Imperative verb 'Call' ke aage 'to' lagakar non-finite infinitive 'to call' banaya. Tense backshift nahi hua.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The judge ordered the court orderly to call the petitioner immediately.'

trapWarning: THAT CLAUSE DISTRACTOR: Examiner option deta hai: 'The judge ordered that the orderly should call...'. Direct exam grammar mein 'ordered + object + to + V1' sabse standard aur concise format hai.

sentence: Direct: The litigant said to the clerk, "Please provide me an attested copy of the decree."
correctAnswer: The litigant requested the clerk to provide him an attested copy of the decree.

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type & Politeness: Imperative request jisme polite marker 'Please' maujood hai.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb: 'Please' ke karan 'said to' ko 'requested' mein convert kiya.
steps.step3_aspect: Polite Word Drop: 'Please' ko completely drop kar diya gaya (retain karna redundant error hai).
steps.step4_inflection: Pronoun & Infinitive: 1st person object 'me' litigant ke anusaar 'him' bana; verb 'provide' ban gayi 'to provide'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The litigant requested the clerk to provide him an attested copy of the decree.'

trapWarning: REDUNDANCY TRAP: Option: '...requested the clerk to please provide him...'. 'Requested' ke baad 'please' lagana strict grammatical redundancy hai.

sentence: Direct: The senior assistant said to the trainee, "Do not disclose the examination question bank."
correctAnswer: The senior assistant instructed the trainee not to disclose the examination question bank.

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type: Negative imperative command starting with 'Do not'.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb: Procedural instruction hone ke karan 'instructed' (ya 'told') choose kiya.
steps.step3_aspect: Negative Infinitive Syntax: 'Do not + V1' ko convert karne ke liye 'not to + V1' ('not to disclose') banaya.
steps.step4_inflection: Word Order Placement: 'not' particle 'to' se pehle aayega ('not to disclose', NOT '*to not disclose').
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The senior assistant instructed the trainee not to disclose the examination question bank.'

trapWarning: SPLIT INFINITIVE TRAP: Formal examination English mein 'to not disclose' ke bajaye strictly 'not to disclose' standard mana jata hai.

sentence: Direct: The magistrate said to the counsel, "Do not raise irrelevant arguments."
correctAnswer: The magistrate forbade the counsel to raise irrelevant arguments.

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type: Negative imperative order by a judicial authority.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb Selection: Negative command ke liye inherently negative verb 'forbade' choose ki gayi.
steps.step4_inflection: Zero-Negative Infinitive: Kyunki 'forbade' ka matlab hi 'mana kiya' hai, iske baad aane wala infinitive POSITIVE ('to raise') hoga. 'Not' drop ho jayega.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The magistrate forbade the counsel to raise irrelevant arguments.'

trapWarning: DOUBLE NEGATIVE BLUNDER: 'The magistrate forbade the counsel NOT to raise...' exam ka sabse bada trap hai. 'Forbade' ke sath 'not' aate hi option reject karein.

sentence: Direct: Suresh said to his team, "Let's analyze the new service rules together."
correctAnswer: Suresh suggested to his team that they should analyze the new service rules together.

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type: Proposal / mutual suggestion starting with 'Let's'.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb: 'said to' ➔ 'suggested to his team' (suggest ke baad preposition 'to' retain rehta hai).
steps.step3_aspect: Conjunction & Pronoun: Conjunction 'that' lagaya. Suresh aur team ke liye 3rd person plural subject 'they' bana.
steps.step4_inflection: Modal Syntax: Proposal clause mein modal auxiliary 'should' jud gaya: 'they should analyze'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'Suresh suggested to his team that they should analyze the new service rules together.'

trapWarning: SUGGEST TO TRAP: Assertive reporting verb 'tell' ke sath 'to' nahi lagta (told me), lekin 'suggested' ke sath listener aane par 'to' lagta hai: 'suggested to his team'.

sentence: Direct: The clerk said, "Alas! The critical backup hard drive has crashed!"
correctAnswer: The clerk exclaimed with sorrow that the critical backup hard drive had crashed.

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type & Emotion: Exclamatory sentence expressing grief/distress marked by interjection 'Alas!' and exclamation mark (!).
steps.step2_time: Reporting Phrase: 'said' + 'Alas!' transform hokar 'exclaimed with sorrow' ban gaya.
steps.step3_aspect: Interjection Elimination: 'Alas!' drop ho gaya aur declarative conjunction 'that' lagaya.
steps.step4_inflection: Tense Backshift: Present Perfect verb 'has crashed' backshift hokar Past Perfect 'had crashed' ban gayi. Exclamation mark full stop ban gaya.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The clerk exclaimed with sorrow that the critical backup hard drive had crashed.'

trapWarning: EMOTION MISMATCH: Option mein 'exclaimed with joy that the hard drive had crashed' likha ho sakta hai. Contextually sorrow match karna zaroori hai.

sentence: Direct: The elderly litigant said to the judge, "May God bless you with wisdom and health!"
correctAnswer: The elderly litigant prayed that God might bless the judge with wisdom and health.

steps.step1_marker: Sentence Type & Intent: Optative sentence expressing solemn prayer to Almighty God starting with 'May God...'.
steps.step2_time: Reporting Verb: God se prarthna hone ke karan reporting verb 'prayed' lagaya.
steps.step3_aspect: Conjunction & Subject: Conjunction 'that' lagaya, aur divine entity 'God' reported clause ka subject bana.
steps.step4_inflection: Modal Shift & Placement: Modal 'May' backshift hokar 'might' bana aur subject 'God' ke BAAD shift hua ('God might bless'). 2nd person 'you' judge ke anusaar 'the judge' (ya 'him') bana.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Synthesis: 'The elderly litigant prayed that God might bless the judge with wisdom and health.'

trapWarning: INVERTED MIGHT TRAP: Option: 'prayed that might God bless...'. Indirect optative statement order follow karta hai: Subject ('God') pehle aayega, modal ('might') baad mein.
